author: opencode-worker-2
text: TIMEBOX-RELEASED by worker-2 (heft) with the investigation complete and the scope now precisely known. FINDINGS: (1) Python/Rust parity EXISTS and is verified - python/tests/coap/test_senml_location_vectors.py and rust/lichen-senml/tests/location_vectors.rs both consume test/vectors/senml_location.json byte-exactly (f64 CBOR, 0xfb values) and pass. (2) The C/Zephyr side CANNOT reach byte parity today: the encoder stores f32 and emits zcbor_float32_put (senml.c:295, API takes float), and the C DECODER rejects the committed oracle bytes entirely - senml_decode_cbor(oracle cbor_hex) returns nonzero (verified empirically at lichen/tests/senml/main.c with a hardcode-and-decode probe; the oracle f64 floats are the likely unsupported element, possibly also zcbor-stub config). (3) The C host suite (lichen/tests/senml) also hits the strnlen minimal-libc break at senml.c:43 (fix pattern: y0z0/wmae memchr helper) and needs a clang-only flag guard for -Wno-error=implicit-int-conversion under gcc. REMAINING WORK (bigger than one round): decide the f64-conformance question per spec appendix-senml (mandate f64 in the C encoder+decoder for parity, or standardize f32 across impls + regenerate the oracle at f32 - the latter is a spec-level regression requiring Mark's call), implement C decoder f64 support (zcbor config or manual), then add the C parity test consuming senml_location.json (the decode-oracle-then-compare-fields design from this round's probe). A working sketch of the parity test existed but was reverted with the decoder gap unresolved.
